stem: A mortality rate measures which epidemiologic quantity about deaths?

options.label: A
options.text: Proportion of people with a disease who die from it
options.misconception: Confuses a population mortality rate with case-fatality, which is restricted to cases.
options.explanation: Deaths among people who have a disease, divided by those cases, is the case-fatality rate; its denominator is cases, not the population.

options.label: B
options.text: Frequency of death in a defined population over an interval
options.misconception: None — a mortality rate is death frequency in a defined population over an interval.
options.explanation: CDC defines a mortality rate as the frequency of occurrence of death in a defined population during a specified interval.

options.label: C
options.text: Proportion of all deaths that are due to one cause
options.misconception: Confuses a mortality rate with proportionate mortality, whose denominator is total deaths.
options.explanation: The share of all deaths due to one cause is proportionate mortality; its denominator is deaths, so it is not a rate of death in a population.

options.label: D
options.text: Years of potential life lost before a reference age
options.misconception: Confuses death frequency with years of potential life lost, a premature-death burden measure.
options.explanation: Years of potential life lost weights each death by how early it occurs, measuring premature mortality rather than how often death occurs.

options.label: E
options.text: Probability that a newly diagnosed patient survives five years
options.misconception: Confuses a population mortality rate with survival among diagnosed patients.
options.explanation: Five-year survival is the probability a diagnosed patient is alive at five years, a prognosis measure within a patient group.

context: Learning objective: A mortality rate measures how often death occurs in a defined population during a specified interval.
